description: LATERAL over a table function, correlating to a column of a preceding table. LATERAL takes the BARE call: FROM t, LATERAL FLATTEN(...) and FROM t, TABLE(FLATTEN(...)) are the two supported spellings, while LATERAL TABLE(FLATTEN(...)) is a syntax error that gets no further than the keyword - the original Java class was written entirely in that third spelling, which Frostlake accepted and no account parses, so every query here is also a test that the supported form is the one being exercised. FLATTEN's INPUT is a VARIANT column for the same reason: a VARCHAR one is refused live however much its text looks like JSON. GENERATOR's ROWCOUNT is not correlatable - Snowflake answers "argument 1 to function GENERATOR needs to be constant" unless its optimiser can fold the value, which is a property of the planner rather than of the language - so the row-multiplication tests use the spelling every account runs: a join to a numbers set built from a CONSTANT rowcount. Converted 1:1 from functions/LateralTableFunctionTest (now retired); the syntax-error offsets are the ones the Java computed from each statement with indexOf.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE numbers (n INTEGER)
INSERT INTO numbers VALUES (2)
INSERT INTO numbers VALUES (3)

SELECT n.n
FROM numbers n
JOIN (SELECT SEQ4() AS k FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 10))) g ON g.k < n.n
ORDER BY n.n
CREATE TABLE data (id INTEGER, tag_list VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO data VALUES (1, 'red,blue,green')
INSERT INTO data VALUES (2, 'small,medium')

SELECT d.id, s.VALUE as tag
FROM data d, LATERAL SPLIT_TO_TABLE(d.tag_list, ',') s
ORDER BY d.id, s.INDEX
CREATE TABLE documents (id INTEGER, json_data VARIANT)
INSERT INTO documents SELECT 1, PARSE_JSON('{"a":1,"b":2}')
INSERT INTO documents SELECT 2, PARSE_JSON('{"x":10}')

SELECT d.id, IFF(f.KEY IS NULL, 'null', 'set')
FROM documents d, LATERAL FLATTEN(INPUT => d.json_data) f
ORDER BY d.id, f.SEQ
SELECT f.KEY FROM documents d, LATERAL FLATTEN(INPUT => d.json_data) f WHERE d.id = 2
CREATE TABLE numbers (n INTEGER)
INSERT INTO numbers VALUES (2)

SELECT n.n
FROM numbers n
CROSS JOIN LATERAL GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => n.n) g
CREATE TABLE ranges (id INTEGER, count INTEGER)
INSERT INTO ranges VALUES (1, 5)
INSERT INTO ranges VALUES (2, 3)

SELECT r.id
FROM ranges r
JOIN (SELECT SEQ4() AS k FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 10))) g ON g.k < r.count
WHERE r.id = 1
CREATE TABLE items (item_id INTEGER, item_name VARCHAR, count INTEGER)
INSERT INTO items VALUES (1, 'Apple', 2)
INSERT INTO items VALUES (2, 'Banana', 3)
INSERT INTO items VALUES (3, 'Cherry', 1)

SELECT i.item_name
FROM items i
JOIN (SELECT SEQ4() AS k FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 10))) g ON g.k < i.count
ORDER BY i.item_id
CREATE TABLE groups (group_id INTEGER, size INTEGER)
INSERT INTO groups VALUES (1, 3)
INSERT INTO groups VALUES (2, 2)

SELECT g.group_id, COUNT(*) as row_count
FROM groups g
JOIN (SELECT SEQ4() AS k FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 10))) gen ON gen.k < g.size
GROUP BY g.group_id
ORDER BY g.group_id
CREATE TABLE nested_data (id INTEGER, data VARIANT)
INSERT INTO nested_data SELECT 1, PARSE_JSON('[1,2,3]')

SELECT n.id, f.VALUE
FROM nested_data n, LATERAL FLATTEN(INPUT => n.data) f
CREATE TABLE source (id INTEGER, value VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO source VALUES (1, 'a,b')
INSERT INTO source VALUES (2, 'c,d')

SELECT s.id, sp.VALUE
FROM source s
CROSS JOIN LATERAL SPLIT_TO_TABLE(s.value, ',') sp
WHERE s.id = 1

INSERT INTO empty_test VALUES (2, 2)

SELECT e.id
FROM empty_test e
JOIN (SELECT SEQ4() AS k FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 10))) g ON g.k < e.count
